blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). The r418-r421 shutdown hang (NativeRuntime::shutdown()'s unconditional, timeout-less thread.join() blocking forever on a worker thread stuck acquiring the global g_dpc_level_mutex inside KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel, orphaned when GuestThreadTerminated unwinds a thread between its Raise and matching Lower) is FIXED and LIVE-VERIFIED (r422). Fix: kept g_dpc_level_mutex as a real cross-thread mutex (preserves r191's deliberate mutual-exclusion semantic across real concurrent host threads -- did not make IRQL thread_local, which would have silently broken that guarantee) but added raise_dpc_level()/lower_dpc_level()/release_residual_dpc_level() (native/include/ac6/native_guest_threads.h, native/src/native_guest_threads.cpp) with a thread_local depth counter, so every GuestThreadTerminated catch site (the ExCreateThread worker in tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py, and both catch blocks in ac6recomp_main.cpp's entry thread) releases whatever IRQL depth that thread still holds instead of orphaning the mutex. Verified live: 4 independent standalone (non-gdb) launches all exit cleanly (exit=0) within their configured probe window, including one with AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE=1 -- the original r418 trigger, retested and confirmed fixed. Native ctest 10/10, tests/test_materialize_native_import_stubs.py 105/105 (three assertions updated for the new wiring), full product pytest 222 passed/1 pre-existing skip. Repo gates and root ctest green (same pre-existing unrelated ac6-cpp-complexity failure). No known blocker remains anywhere in the r399-r422 chain. Named for r423 (lowest-cost open thread, not a blocker): add a targeted unit/integration test that directly simulates 'raised IRQL then GuestThreadTerminated' to cover this regression class going forward. Separately, r418's presented_frames=0/present=0 question (the per-frame loop runs but the guest never emits a Present packet in the observed window) remains open as the next PRODUCT question, now uncomplicated by any shutdown hang. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched -- reports and named tool/source changes for r413-r422 were committed individually, the broader tree state was not.
